items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: he started singing, Jack Carey, Harry Dog on the water.

ctx.x: It's a pretty nice piece. Did any of the tunes have any special names? Well, we call that number one. Yeah, but I mean like the Tiger Rag, did it have another name? Oh, Tiger Rag, that's all. We called it. Did it have any words? That's one thing.

Well, yeah, the people out in the audience started singing. When we were playing, when we got to that last spot, they said, Jack Carey on the water, selling pork chops, two for a quarter, you know. It just kept on going like that. They made a song, I assume. I couldn't remember it all. All I knew there was a party at the corner of Third Wood at a grocery store. And every time we'd go to the National Park on Monday nights past that, he started singing, Jack Carey, Harry Dog on the water. Jack Carey could sing that…
